tierJustification: instrument repair on my own harness, no money path and no product change; reviewer tier not claimed
headline: CONF-02's cost mechanism was never armed by my harness: API-placed orders collect zero excursion samples, and my order-loop timer was reading a frame with no book. Both fixed; the running duration gate now reads 14,652 excursion samples and attributes loop cost to the frame that holds the trades.

finding1_excursion_sampling_was_silent.claim: Every order my harness placed through orderService.submitOrder was excursion-free, so a run could accumulate closed trades that cost nothing to carry.
finding1_excursion_sampling_was_silent.instrument: CONF-02 duration gate (scripts/conf01-duration-gate.mjs) heavy-field reader, plus source reading of order-manager.js
finding1_excursion_sampling_was_silent.mechanism: order-manager.js:3916-3920 _calculateExcursionRValues reads array_base_price ?? openPrice and initialStopLoss ?? initial_sl ?? stopLoss. If either is not finite it returns null and _appendExcursionSnapshot (5943) no-ops, so the per-bar sample arrays are never created. Sampling is otherwise driven per closed bar from updatePositions (32133, entry bar excluded) and post-exit (31377, 31406).

before.note: order-accumulation census W93 and the first CONF-02 gate launch

finding1_excursion_sampling_was_silent.fix: cycleTrades now sends openPrice, array_base_price and initialStopLoss with the market order (scripts/lib/conf01-session.mjs)
finding1_excursion_sampling_was_silent.consequence: The per-tick cost of carrying closed trades could not have been measured before this fix. Any earlier per-tick figure of mine is a measurement of the cheap configuration - the third time this campaign has done that, and the second time I did it to myself.

finding2_order_loop_attribution_defect.claim: My order-loop timer reported the cost of the wrong frame.

perFrameAtSample4.note: holds all 24 closed trades; updatePositions does not tick

evidence.why: the frame I place orders into exhausts its resident replay window and stalls (replayAfter.isPlaying=false at idx 2011), while peer panels keep ticking with empty books

finding2_order_loop_attribution_defect.fix: measureOrderLoopCost now reports isHost, timeframe, closedHere, openHere and excursionSamplesHere per frame, and exposes measured = the ticking frame with the largest book. A level is valid only if that frame ticks, holds closed trades, and excursion samples exist.
finding2_order_loop_attribution_defect.voids: scripts/order-accumulation-census.mjs results from W93 (0.5-0.74 ms/tick, flat to 42 closed trades). Do not quote them. Re-runs after the duration gate finishes.
finding2_order_loop_attribution_defect.openQuestion: with the book frame ticking and ~188 samples per closed trade, the per-tick cost may be materially higher than 0.012 ms; the number A needs for POST-EXIT-SAMPLING-CUT is not yet measured

finding3_element_count_climbs_with_close.note: n=4 and not monotonic at sample 4; a slope with confidence follows from the full run under DUR-01 rather than an eyeball on four points

liveRunState.gate: TALARIA_FREEZE_GATE default -> CONF-01 duration gate via scripts/freeze-gate.mjs
liveRunState.compliance: four panels, four symbols, four timeframes, indicators loaded, orders accumulating; advancing 4/4 at samples 1, 2 and 4
liveRunState.caveat: sample 3 read advancing=0/4 and renderer 29.3%; peer panels exhaust their resident window and are re-seeked between samples, so the CPU series carries stall points that must be excluded, not averaged

instrumentScope: Renderer JS heap is ~21% of the page renderer and ~10% of all Chrome (INSTRUMENT-SCOPE-V1). Footprint figures in this run are OS PrivateMemorySize64 across all Chrome processes and do see the rest.
